name: The Signposted Oak of Jardin des Plantes
access: Free, public botanical garden (Jardin des Plantes, 7 hectares, open daily)
transport: Central Toulouse; Toulouse metro Line B, Palais de Justice or Carmes station, then a short walk (exact stop not independently verified this pass)
verify_notes: Toulouse Metropole's own urban tree inventory (Ville de Toulouse remarkable-label source) records this as a Quercus robur at a point roughly 90m from the Jardin des Plantes garden centroid. OpenStreetMap independently carries a mapped point at essentially this same coordinate named 'Chene pedoncule' (Pedunculate Oak) tagged as a tourism/information feature, i.e. a community-mapped, signposted specimen tree, which is a real independent corroboration of both existence and species even though it does not give an age. Single formal source for age (none found) - flag. Jardin des Plantes is a 7ha public botanical garden on Allee Jules-Guesde, part of a connected green corridor with Jardin Royal and Jardin du Grand Rond (see tls_002/tls_003 nearby).

verify_notes: Toulouse Metropole's urban tree inventory places this Ulmus glabra at a point reverse-geocoding to 'Boulingrin', the informal name for the Jardin du Grand Rond, a large public roundabout garden (approx 200m diameter) connected to Jardin des Plantes and Jardin Royal, all on Allee Jules-Guesde. name: The Osage Orange of the Grand Rond

location.address: Near Boulingrin / Jardin du Grand Rond, Allee Jules-Guesde area

access: Free, public garden area (Boulingrin / Jardin du Grand Rond)
transport: Central Toulouse; Toulouse metro Line B, Palais de Justice or Carmes station, then a short walk (exact stop not independently verified this pass)
verify_notes: Toulouse Metropole's urban tree inventory places this Maclura pomifera near Boulingrin/Jardin du Grand Rond, about 250m from tls_002. Osage Orange is an unusual, visually distinctive tree (fissured orange-brown bark, large inedible knobbly fruit) rarely seen this far from North America, which is likely why the city flagged it remarkable; the Jardin Royal nearby is independently reported (Wikipedia) to hold an Osage Orange among its rare specimens, so this is plausibly that same tradition of unusual plantings across the connected Jardin Royal/Grand Rond/Jardin des Plantes corridor, though not confirmed as the exact same tree Wikipedia refers to. Single-sourced beyond the register for this specific tree; no age found.

name: The Grieving Hackberry of Terre-Cabade

location.address: Cimetiere de Terre-Cabade, 1 Avenue du Cimetiere

transport: Guilhemery / Cote Pavee district, north-east of the centre; nearest metro/tram stop not verified this pass
verify_notes: Strong match: France3 Region's 2025 survey of Toulouse's remarkable trees (classified 'arbre exceptionnel' in Haute-Garonne by the association Arbres et Paysages d'Autan) describes a Celtis australis (micocoulier) that has grown between two gravestones in the Terre-Cabade cemetery, over 4 metres in circumference, 26 metres tall, its leaves changing shape through the day to cope with heat. The register's coordinate for id 21671 sits within about 45 metres of the cemetery's published address coordinate, essentially the same spot. Genuinely remarkable specimen with real visual character (growing wedged between two graves); age not given by any source but the girth (4m+) implies a mature, long-established tree. Two independent sources (city register + independent press survey), so this is the best-evidenced Toulouse tree in this batch.

name: The Plane of Place Anatole France
access: Free, public square (Place Anatole France, Saint-Cyprien)

verify_notes: Toulouse Metropole's urban tree inventory places this Platanus x hispanica (register spelling; the corpus's canonical common name is London Plane, Platanus x acerifolia, the same hybrid) at Place Anatole France in Saint-Cyprien. Register records the species as Platanus x.hispanica specifically, which some authorities treat as a synonym of x acerifolia and others as the more geographically apt name for the same widely-planted hybrid plane; used the corpus's existing canonical form per house style. Single-sourced beyond the register; no age found. Development stage '3 - Adulte'. NOTE: this is a different plane tree from the famous 'bois de loupe' (burl growth) specimen in Jardin Royal reported by France3 Regions in 2025 - that tree's location does not match this or any other candidate in this pass's register set closely enough to confirm identity, so it is not claimed here; see leads for that gap.
